Title: Red Sea and Umrah, 14 nights in Jeddah, Makkah and Madinah
Teaser: All inclusive days on Obhur Bay, then five nights beside each Holy Mosque
Property: Rixos Obhur Jeddah, Hilton Suites Jabal Omar Makkah and InterContinental Dar Al Hijra Madinah
Board: All inclusive in Jeddah, breakfast in Makkah and Madinah
Map address: Rixos Obhur Jeddah Resort & Villas, Obhur, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
Description:
Two weeks that give you both halves of a trip to Saudi Arabia. You start on the Red Sea at Rixos Obhur Jeddah, the city's first luxury all inclusive resort, where every meal, drink and snack is covered and the beach is a few steps from your room. Then you move inland for ten nights of Umrah, five beside the Haram in Makkah and five beside the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah.
Both holy city hotels were chosen for the walk. Hilton Suites Jabal Omar Makkah sits around 300 metres from Masjid al-Haram by the King Fahad gate, close enough to return between prayers rather than build your day around one visit. InterContinental Dar Al Hijra Madinah is a two minute walk from Masjid an-Nabawi, with rooms looking out over the city and Mount Uhud.
Flights are with Etihad Airways from London Heathrow through Abu Dhabi, and every transfer in between is included, so the only thing you arrange after you land is your own time. Book by 30 September for travel in November.
Country description: Saudi Arabia has opened up quickly for visitors, and one trip can now hold both a beach week and Umrah. Jeddah is the relaxed coastal city, with the Red Sea on its doorstep, the restored old town at Al Balad and a corniche made for evening walks. Makkah is about an hour inland by road, and the Haramain high speed railway covers Makkah to Madinah in roughly two hours. November brings warm days and cooler evenings, which is comfortable weather for long spells on foot.
Itinerary:
Nights 1 to 4, Jeddah. Rixos Obhur Jeddah Resort & Villas on Obhur Bay, all inclusive. A private beach, pools, a spa and one of the liveliest kids' clubs in the country, with King Abdulaziz International Airport around half an hour away.
Nights 5 to 9, Makkah. Hilton Suites Jabal Omar Makkah, room and breakfast. Around 300 metres from Masjid al-Haram, a walk of four to five minutes to the King Fahad gate.
Nights 10 to 14, Madinah. InterContinental Dar Al Hijra Madinah, room and breakfast. Roughly 300 metres from Masjid an-Nabawi, near enough to be there in two minutes.
Airport and intercity transfers are included throughout, Jeddah to Makkah and Makkah to Madinah included.
Highlights:
Jeddah's first luxury all inclusive resort, on the Red Sea
Five nights within a five minute walk of Masjid al-Haram
Five nights two minutes from the Prophet's Mosque
Every transfer included, airport to hotel and city to city
Etihad Airways from London Heathrow

Title: 10 nights in Qatar, a desert villa and a private island
Teaser: Two nights in a tented pool villa on the Inland Sea, then eight at the Ritz-Carlton
Property: The Outpost Al Barari and The Ritz-Carlton, Doha
Map address: The Ritz-Carlton, Doha, West Bay Lagoon, Doha, Qatar
Description:
Ten nights that show both sides of Qatar. You begin in the desert at The Outpost Al Barari, a camp of twenty one tented villas inside the Inland Sea nature reserve, where most villas have their own pool and the nearest streetlight is a long way off. Two nights is enough for a dune drive, a farm to table dinner and a night under a sky you will not get in the city.
Then you come back north to The Ritz-Carlton, Doha, which sits on its own private island in West Bay Lagoon with a beach, a large marina, a spa and a kids' club. Eight nights there leaves room for the Museum of Islamic Art, Souq Waqif and the Corniche without any of it feeling rushed.
Qatar Airways flies direct from London Heathrow, so you land in Doha in under seven hours. Breakfast and every transfer are included, the run south to the reserve and back among them.
Country description: Qatar is small enough to cross in a morning, which is what makes a two centre trip work here. Doha holds the museums, the souq and the waterfront, and an hour south the land empties into the dunes of Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea, a protected reserve where the desert runs straight into the water. January is the best month to go, with warm days, cool evenings and clear skies.
Itinerary:
Nights 1 and 2, the Inland Sea. The Outpost Al Barari at Mesaieed, about an hour south of Hamad International Airport, in a tented villa with breakfast. Camel rides, dune buggies, electric fat bikes and a desert spa are all on site.
Nights 3 to 10, Doha. The Ritz-Carlton, Doha on its private island in West Bay Lagoon, room and breakfast. A private beach island, a 235 berth marina, The Ritz-Carlton Spa and the Ritz Kids club.
Airport transfers and the transfer between the two hotels are included.
Highlights:
Direct Qatar Airways flights from London Heathrow
A tented villa with its own pool inside the Khor Al Adaid reserve
Eight nights on a private island with a beach and a marina
Breakfast and all transfers included
Museum of Islamic Art, Souq Waqif and the Corniche within easy reach

Title: 13 nights in Doha, Madinah and Makkah with Saudia
Teaser: Three nights at The Plaza Doha, then ten beside the two Holy Mosques
Property: The Plaza Doha LXR Hotels & Resorts, Pullman ZamZam Madinah and Jabal Omar Marriott Hotel Makkah
Urgency: Free afternoon tea at The Plaza Doha, for a limited time
Map address: The Plaza Doha, LXR Hotels & Resorts, Doha, Qatar
Description:
Thirteen nights that open with a city break and close with Umrah. The first three are at The Plaza Doha, an LXR hotel in the centre of the city, minutes from the National Museum of Qatar and a short drive from Souq Waqif. Book this one and afternoon tea there is on us, for a limited time and exclusive to Halal World Travel.
From Doha you travel on to Madinah for five nights at Pullman ZamZam, which stands about 150 metres from Masjid an-Nabawi. Then five more in Makkah at the Jabal Omar Marriott, a three minute walk from the King Fahad gate of Masjid al-Haram. Both are near enough that you can go back for every prayer rather than pick one.
Flights are with Saudia from London Heathrow and breakfast is included at all three hotels.
Country description: March suits this trip. Doha sits in the mid twenties, warm enough for the Corniche in the evening without the summer heat, and both holy cities are comfortable for long spells outdoors. The Haramain high speed railway links Madinah, Jeddah and Makkah in around two hours, which keeps the Saudi half of the journey simple.
Itinerary:
Nights 1 to 3, Doha. The Plaza Doha, LXR Hotels & Resorts, room and breakfast, with a complimentary afternoon tea while the offer lasts. Indoor and outdoor pools, a wellness centre and three restaurants.
Nights 4 to 8, Madinah. Pullman ZamZam Madinah, room and breakfast, around 150 metres from Masjid an-Nabawi and the Rawdah.
Nights 9 to 13, Makkah. Jabal Omar Marriott Hotel Makkah, room and breakfast, a three minute walk to the King Fahad gate through the Jabal Omar complex. Many rooms look out over Masjid Al Haram and the city.
Highlights:
Free afternoon tea at The Plaza Doha, exclusive to Halal World Travel
Three nights in central Doha before you travel on
Five nights around 150 metres from the Prophet's Mosque
Five nights three minutes from the gates of Masjid al-Haram
Saudia flights from London Heathrow, breakfast at all three hotels

Title: 10 nights in Zanzibar, two coasts on half board
Teaser: Five nights on the cliffs at Mangapwani, five on the sand at Pwani Mchangani
Property: Sea Cliff Resort & Spa Zanzibar and LUX* Marijani Zanzibar
Map address: Sea Cliff Resort & Spa Zanzibar, Mangapwani, Zanzibar, Tanzania
Description:
Zanzibar is a small island, but its coasts are not the same as one another, so this trip gives you both. The first five nights are at Sea Cliff Resort & Spa on the north west side at Mangapwani, set on a cliff above the Indian Ocean with infinity pools, the Zuri Rituals spa and the island's only golf course. Stone Town is about twenty five minutes down the road when you want the spice market and the old carved doors.
The second five are at LUX* Marijani on the north east coast at Pwani Mchangani, a smaller place of eighty two rooms with Arab and Swahili touches, an infinity pool and a private stretch of one of the best beaches on the island. Sunrise on that side, sunset back at Sea Cliff, which is a fair reason to take them in that order.
Half board at both hotels covers breakfast and dinner, so the days are yours. Flights are with Etihad Airways from London Heathrow through Abu Dhabi.
Country description: Zanzibar lies off the coast of Tanzania in the Indian Ocean, close enough to the equator that the sea stays warm all year round. Stone Town, the old trading port at its heart, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and worth a day of anyone's holiday for the spice market, the seafront and the carved doors. The island is predominantly Muslim, so halal food is the norm rather than a request, and modest dress away from the resorts is appreciated.
Itinerary:
Nights 1 to 5, Mangapwani. Sea Cliff Resort & Spa Zanzibar on the north west coast, half board. A cliff top setting above the Indian Ocean, infinity pools, a private beach, horse riding, tennis and Zanzibar's only golf course, with Stone Town around twenty five minutes away.
Nights 6 to 10, Pwani Mchangani. LUX* Marijani Zanzibar on the north east coast, half board. Eighty two rooms, two restaurants, a private beach, an infinity pool and the LUX* ME Spa.
Highlights:
Two coasts in one holiday, north west cliffs and north east sand
Half board at both hotels, breakfast and dinner included
Zanzibar's only golf course, at Sea Cliff
A private beach at Pwani Mchangani, one of the finest on the island
Etihad Airways from London Heathrow
